asOf: Close of Thursday 1 October 2026 for equities, sectors, bonds, factors and the Treasury curve, with index levels, commodities, currencies and crypto to 05:44 UTC on Friday 2 October. Weekend edition: next refresh Monday 5 October

read.headline: October went from 70% to 25% in four sessions. The long end priced none of it.
read.standfirst: Weekend edition. The week's front end was job openings at a five-month low, consumer confidence at a 2014 low, a core PCE that printed 3.0% after the BEA rewrote July, and two members of the Fed's leadership — Williams on Tuesday, Jefferson on Thursday — saying the committee can wait: October's hike went from more than 70% priced on Monday to about 25% on Thursday and the two-year fell from 4.96% to 4.79%. The week's long end was final Q2 GDP revised to 2.2%, a Chicago PMI of 58.8, ISM prices paid at 77.9, a 4.4% Brent rally on China's fuel-export halt and a third US carrier group, gilts at a 28-year high and Bunds at a 2009 high: the ten-year touched 5.344% on Thursday, its highest since 2002, before closing at 5.233%. Equities fell three days to a two-week low and bounced 0.19% on Thursday; the S&P 500 ETF is down 0.95% over five sessions, technology +0.78% and energy +1.06% the only sectors up. The dollar index is 102.08, a 17-month high and a third weekly gain; the euro $1.1237 on France's budget. Overnight Tokyo core CPI printed 2.7% against 2.4%, the Nikkei gave back 0.96% of Thursday's 3.24%, Hong Kong reopened 2.64% lower, China is shut until the 8th. Payrolls at 08:30 ET, seen near 90,000.

points.title: The week in the curve: the two-year fell 17bp from its high, the ten-year ended 3bp higher.
points.text: The three-month bill is 4.17%, the two-year 4.78%, the ten-year 5.24%, the twenty-year 5.64% and the thirty-year 5.61%; two-tens is 46bp from 32bp on Monday and bill-to-ten 107bp. The move was all at the front: October's hike odds fell from more than 70% to about 25% across Williams' 'no need for urgency', the 3.0% core PCE and Jefferson's 'may take time', while Logan said after Thursday's close that policy has been 'offsides' and rates need to rise half a point or more. The long end heard the other half of the week — GDP 2.2%, Chicago PMI 58.8, ISM prices paid 77.9, Brent +4.4% — and the ten-year touched 5.344% before Thursday's 5.9bp fall, its biggest in over a month. In the funds the 20-year-plus Treasury is down 2.03% over five sessions, 5.17% over a month and 13.22% over twelve; the 3–7 year fund rose 0.29% on Thursday and TIPS 0.26% while high yield fell 0.40% and emerging-market bonds 0.64%, down 2.08% on the week. Saxo's Charu Chanana put it plainly: long yields rising while hike odds fall is term premium and fiscal risk, not the next Fed decision. Next week has the three-year, ten-year and thirty-year auctions, the first at these levels.

points.title: Technology and energy were the only sectors up on the week. Micron and a $4 Brent rally explain both.
points.text: Over five sessions technology is +0.78% and energy +1.06%; everything else is red, communication services −2.67%, health care −2.64%, materials −2.53%, financials −2.52%. Thursday itself had technology +1.05% and energy +1.95% leading, health care −1.32% lagging; the Philadelphia semiconductor index rose 1.59% with Micron +3.03% after its beat and Nvidia +1.09% to its highest since mid-May, while Alphabet fell 1.7% and Broadcom 2.15%. The S&P 500 closed at 7,666.45, up 0.19%, snapping a three-day slide that had taken it to a two-week low; the VIX is 16.39, up 10.22% on the week. The month's column is still September's: technology +7.74% is the only sector positive, materials −8.33%, financials −7.28%, utilities −7.01% and real estate −6.97% the worst; over three months energy +17.81% and technology +9.54% against utilities −13.29% and industrials −8.30%. In the factors, momentum beat the index by 0.94% on Thursday and 1.70% on the week, buybacks by 0.95%, mid-caps by 0.86%; growth is 3.37% ahead over a month and value 3.29% behind, private equity 9.55% behind. After the close Nike beat on earnings, missed on revenue, cut its full-year guide and announced a restructuring; the shares fell 6–9%.

points.title: Brent rose 4.37% on Thursday. The five-day column still says −2.17%, and that is the roll.
points.text: December Brent settled $4.28 higher at $102.31 and WTI $2.45 higher at $92.87 after Chinese refiners suspended product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, PetroChina cancelled gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes, the Wall Street Journal reported the Pentagon may send a third carrier group and 10,000 personnel to the Gulf, Iran's strait authority said several tankers had been attacked, and Trump said strikes were 'possible' after the midterms. This morning Brent is $102.06, down 0.24%, and WTI $92.46, down 0.44%. Read the columns carefully: Brent's five-day −2.17% and one-month +6.72% still straddle Wednesday's November expiry at $103.53, so the December contract has actually risen about 6% since Tuesday's $96.30 low; WTI, which did not roll, is flat on the week. Barclays raised its fourth-quarter Brent forecast by $20 to $115 and 2026 to $100; Goldman still has $85 at year-end with exports near pre-war. Energy equities rose 1.95% and are up 40.24% this year. Natural gas is $2.92, down 8.64% on the week; gasoline +8.40% over a month; heating oil $4.61, still up 116.05% in 2026 with refined-product exports the gap the war has not closed.

points.title: Europe fell harder than anywhere on Thursday: a bond rout, a French budget and a 28-year gilt high.
points.text: Italy fell 2.52%, Spain 2.26%, France 2.09%, the Netherlands 1.67%, the UK 1.38% and Germany 1.19% in dollar terms; the Stoxx 600 closed at 626.65, down 1.30%, its lowest since June, the FTSE 100 lost 1.68%, the CAC 1.62%, the FTSE MIB 2.21% and the DAX 1.03% as gilt yields hit a 28-year high, the Bund traded near 3.65%, its highest since 2009, and France presented a 2027 budget with €54 billion of savings that a minority government may not pass. The developed ex-US fund lost 1.03% on the day and 2.60% on the week; over a month France is −8.51%, Switzerland −6.47%, Italy −6.74%. Elsewhere Korea rose 1.82% and Turkey 1.78% while Mexico fell 1.86% and Argentina 2.14%, the latter −13.85% over a month; South Africa is −10.19% and Indonesia −10.69% over the same period. Over twelve months Korea is +122.81% and Taiwan +76.22%. This morning the Nikkei is down 0.96% near 68,300 after adding more than 3,400 points in two days, the Hang Seng reopened 2.64% lower on property and tech, the Kospi is up 0.1%, Australia 0.57%, Taiwan 0.25%; Shanghai is shut until 8 October and India for Gandhi Jayanti.

points.title: The dollar's third weekly gain took it to a 17-month high. The yen is the only major fighting back.
points.text: The dollar index is 102.08, up about 1% on the week and its third straight weekly gain, a run last seen in May 2025. EUR/USD is 1.13, down 1.15% over five sessions and 2.88% over a month, after touching $1.1237, its lowest since May 2025, on France's budget and the bond sell-off — the euro-area inflation prints that should have helped it did not, because October's ECB odds halved to about 30% anyway. The dollar gained 3.01% on the peso this week and 7.59% over a month, 1.95% on the rand, 0.78% on the real; the kiwi is 4.01% weaker over a month and the Australian dollar 3.15%, at 69 cents. USD/JPY is 157.83, down 0.14% after Tokyo core CPI printed 2.7% against 2.4% expected with the core-core measure at 3.0%, putting a BoJ October move back in the conversation a day after the cautious summary of opinions; the pair is down 2.17% over three months, the only major the dollar lost to in the quarter. The won is 11.47% stronger over three months. In crypto Bitcoin is $86,127, up 1.51% on the day and 1.97% on the week, Solana +3.07% and Litecoin +3.14% on the day; Chainlink is +81.95% over three months, Cardano −70.97% over twelve.

points.title: Gold held $4,218 as the bill rate fell. Silver lost 4.89% on the week; sugar gained 8.23%.
points.text: Gold is $4,217.80, up 0.37% on the day but down 2.39% on the week and 4.46% over a month, held by Thursday's Treasury rally and the Bank of Korea's plan to start buying in December against a dollar at a 17-month high; over twelve months it is +9.04%. Silver is $61.63, down 4.89% on the week and 15.48% over six months while +32.92% over a year; platinum rose 1.27% to $1,751.85. Copper is $6.59, down 2.61% on the week and flat over a month, +33.13% over a year; aluminium rose 0.82% but is 6.26% lower on the week. In the crops the week belongs to sugar, +8.23%, and coffee, +3.46%, against cotton −6.59% after two limit-down sessions, corn −5.13%, cocoa −4.24% and 14.22% lower over a month, wheat −12.08% over a month. Lean hogs are −30.20% over three months, the worst row on the board. Natural gas at $2.92 is down 8.64% on the week and 19.27% this year, the one energy contract the war has not lifted.

curve.title: The US Treasury curve
curve.note: Today against a month ago, at the end of a week in which the two ends of the curve told different stories. The two-year touched 4.96% on Tuesday morning and closed Thursday at 4.79%, down 9.6bp on the day, as October's hike went from more than 70% priced to about 25% on Williams, a soft PCE and Jefferson; the ten-year touched 5.344% on Thursday, its highest since 2002, before closing at 5.233%, down 5.9bp, its biggest fall in over a month, and the thirty-year 5.616% after a 5.642% high on Wednesday. The source table prints 4.78%, 5.24% and 5.61%. September was still the ten-year's worst month since 2022; the one-month column is all red. Coupon supply returns next week: three-year on Tuesday, ten-year on Wednesday, thirty-year on Thursday, the first auctions at these levels.

spreads.label: 2s10s
spreads.note: 46bp from 41bp on Wednesday, 37bp on Tuesday and 32bp on Monday — 14bp of steepening in a week, almost all of it the two-year falling. The front end has priced the Fed out of October; the ten-year closed the week 3bp higher than it started it.

spreads.label: 3M10Y
spreads.note: 107bp from 109bp on Wednesday, still above 100 for a third day and the widest stretch of the cycle. The bill at 4.17% is where it was before the September hike was priced; the ten-year at 5.24% is 30bp higher than it was then.

spreads.label: 10s30s
spreads.note: 37bp from 35bp. The long bond gave back 2.3bp on Thursday after seven sessions higher; the twenty-year at 5.64% remains the highest point on the curve. Logan said after the close that higher yields may partly be term premium — and that rates still need to rise half a point or more.

groups.title: Equities by country
groups.note: Country ETF prices in US dollars at Thursday's New York close. Europe fell hardest on the bond rout and France's budget — Italy −2.52%, Spain −2.26%, France −2.09% — while Korea +1.82% and Turkey +1.78% rose. The five-day column is the week: only Brazil, Korea's three-month and the US's year-to-date columns look comfortable. Friday morning: Nikkei −0.96%, Hang Seng −2.64% on reopening, Kospi +0.1%; China shut until 8 October, India shut Friday.

groups.title: US sectors
groups.note: The eleven S&P sector SPDRs at Thursday's close. Energy +1.95% on the Brent rally and technology +1.05% on the chipmakers led; health care −1.32% and communication services −0.93% lagged. The five-day column is the week: technology and energy are the only two sectors up.

groups.title: Bonds and credit
groups.note: Total-return prices, so a falling number means yields rose. Thursday was the first day in a week the long end rallied: the 3–7 year fund +0.29%, TIPS +0.26%, municipals +0.24%, the 20-year-plus fund −0.09% after touching a 2002 yield high intraday. Every row is red over five days, a month and a year.

groups.title: Commodities
groups.note: Live to 05:44 UTC on Friday. Brent's row is the December contract, which settled 4.37% higher on Thursday at $102.31; its five-day −2.17% and one-month columns still straddle Wednesday's November expiry at $103.53, so the week's real move in December Brent is about +6% from Tuesday's low. WTI did not roll and is flat on the week. Sugar +8.23% and natural gas −8.64% bracket the week.

groups.title: Currencies
groups.note: Live to Friday morning, payrolls day. The dollar index is at a 17-month high after a third weekly gain; the euro touched its lowest since May 2025 on France's budget; the yen firmed on a 2.7% Tokyo core CPI. Read USD/XXX pairs the right way round: a green cell means the dollar gained on that currency, not that the currency did well.
